key_insight: As doping and vacancy defects strongly tune monolayer MoS2 electronic behavior, with As at the Mo site emerging as the most promising modification for optoelectronic applications.
engineering_relevance: These defect-engineering results point to a practical route for designing MoS2-based photocatalysts, photovoltaics, and FET channels with targeted p-type or n-type behavior.
method: DFT calculations on pristine and defected MoS2 monolayers
Compared Mo-vacancy, S-vacancy, As-Mo, As-S, and As-interstitial configurations
Evaluated structural relaxation and electronic band/defect-state changes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports defect-induced midgap states and Fermi-level shifts: V_S, V_Mo, As-Mo, and As-S show p-type behavior, while As interstitial shifts toward n-type.
watch_item: The conclusions come from first-principles defect models, so experimental verification is needed to confirm stability, achievable dopant placement, and real-device performance.
paper_title: First-principles study of the impact of As doping on the structural and electronic properties of MoS$_2$ monolayer
